relevance.reason: It attempts the canteen question but explains design thinking in general terms.

criteria.name: Scenario and users
criteria.evidence: Problem: The canteen needs a mobile app for ordering food.
criteria.issue: Mentions the canteen, but never names the users (students with a class after lunch, counter staff) or the constraint (a short lunch break).
criteria.fix: Open with one line: the LICET canteen at 12:30, students who must reach a 1:10 class, and the counter staff.

criteria.name: Diagram or artefact
criteria.evidence: [Diagram of 5 stages drawn]
criteria.issue: A bare placeholder: no labels, no canteen content, and nothing shows the loop back from Test.
criteria.fix: Draw the five stages as a loop with arrows from Test back to Define and Ideate, and write the canteen activity under each stage.

criteria.name: Concepts and method
criteria.evidence: Define - defining the problem clearly.
criteria.issue: All five stages are named and roughly right, but each gets a one-line textbook gloss. POV and How Might We are never mentioned.
criteria.fix: Explain Define as a POV statement ([user] needs [need] because [insight]) and Ideate as diverge-then-converge.

criteria.name: Application to the scenario
criteria.evidence: Solution: We can make an app so students can order food.
criteria.issue: The stages are never applied to the canteen. The problem is written as a solution ('the canteen needs a mobile app'), which scores 0 for Define, and generic theory caps application at 1.
criteria.fix: Apply each stage to the canteen: who you observed at 12:30, an empathy map with real entries, a POV such as 'a student with a 40-minute break needs a predictable lunch wait', four or more ideas, a paper prototype, a 5-student test.

criteria.name: Justification and outcome
criteria.issue: No reason is given for choosing the app, and nothing says how it would be tested or improved.
criteria.fix: Pick one idea with a stated criterion (impact vs. feasibility) and end with a test: 5 students, a task such as 'order lunch for a 12:40 pickup', a metric, and what you would change.

strengths: Names all five stages in the right order.

nextSteps.action: Rewrite Define as a user need, not a solution: 'A student with a 40-minute lunch break needs to get food predictably because arriving late costs attendance.'
nextSteps.why: A solution written as the problem scores 0 for Define. Ms. Accelia warned about this exact line in the canteen workshop.

nextSteps.action: Apply every stage to the canteen with specific evidence (queue at 12:30, interviews, empathy map entries).
nextSteps.why: Answers that only define the five stages are capped at about 4/10. Application is the 3-mark criterion.

nextSteps.action: Draw the stages as a loop with arrows back from Test, labelled with canteen activities, and end with how you would test and iterate.
nextSteps.why: A diagram with no scenario content gets at most half the diagram marks, and the last 2 marks need a test plan.

cannotVerify: The diagram is only described as '[Diagram of 5 stages drawn]', so its shape and labels can't be checked.
result.summary: This explains design thinking in general but never applies it to the canteen, and it writes the problem as a solution. As it stands it falls in the re-appear band; the three fixes below are worth about 5 marks.

criteria.name: Scenario and users
criteria.evidence: Scenario: LICET canteen, 12:30-1:10 lunch break. Users: students with a class at 1:10, and canteen counter staff.

criteria.name: Diagram or artefact
criteria.evidence: arrows from Test back to Define and Ideate labelled 'iterate'
criteria.issue: The loop and iteration arrows are right, and the empathy map is specific, but the loop itself carries no canteen content.
criteria.fix: Write the canteen activity under each stage of the loop (e.g. 'observe 12:30 queue' under Empathize).

criteria.name: Concepts and method
criteria.evidence: A student with a 40-minute lunch break needs to get food quickly and predictably because arriving late to class costs attendance.

criteria.name: Application to the scenario
criteria.evidence: Observed the queue on 3 days at 12:30 (about 60 students, average wait 14 min) and interviewed 6 students and 2 staff.
criteria.issue: Empathize, Define, Ideate and Test are applied with specific evidence. Prototype is a single line, and the answer doesn't say what the paper prototype was meant to learn.
criteria.fix: Add one line to Prototype: what the paper prototype tests (can students choose a pickup slot in under a minute?).

criteria.name: Justification and outcome
criteria.evidence: Converge using an impact/feasibility matrix: (a) and (b) are high impact and feasible this semester; (d) needs admin approval.
criteria.issue: The idea is chosen with stated criteria and the test has metrics, but none of them measures the original problem: students arriving late.
criteria.fix: Add a success measure tied to the problem, e.g. the share of testers who would reach a 1:10 class on time.

strengths: The POV is a user need with an insight, which is exactly the Define format taught in class.

nextSteps.why: The last 2 marks reward showing the design solves the stated need.

nextSteps.action: Annotate the loop diagram with what happens at each stage in the canteen.
